lyrics:
[Intro: droning open-tuned acoustic guitar, mandolin tremolo]

[Verse 1: raspy, close, quiet]
I've been standing at the edge of every frame
The blur behind the smile, without a name
And I would trade the whole unbroken sky
To be the thing that finally caught your eye

[Pre-Chorus: strings creep in]
'Cause nobody gets the real thing anymore
We send the better version to the door

[Chorus: full band, crashing drums, wide strings]
And if you looked up, you would see me
I'm right here where I've always been
I don't need the world to believe me
I just need one person to let me in
If you looked up
If you looked up

[Verse 2: quieter again, mandolin answers]
I can taste the words I never got to say
They sit behind my teeth like yesterday
You're so close I can hear you breathing slow
And still a thousand miles of glass to go

[Pre-Chorus: strings rise]
And everything I built to keep me safe
Is everything that's standing in the way

[Chorus: full band, crashing drums, wide strings]
And if you looked up, you would see me
I'm right here where I've always been
I don't need the world to believe me
I just need one person to let me in
If you looked up
If you looked up

[Instrumental: mandolin and strings, one stumbling odd bar, building]

[Bridge: voice strains, drums pound]
I don't want to be a light across the bay
A voice inside a wire, a name you save
I want to be the weight beside your hand
The one thing in this life you understand

[Breakdown: guitar and voice only]
If you looked up, you would see me
I've been waving all this time

[Final Chorus: biggest, strings soaring, full cry]
And if you looked up, you would see me
I'm right here where I've always been
Let the whole world never believe me
I just need you to let me in
If you looked up
If you looked up

[Outro: band falls away, mandolin fades]
Look up
I'm right here
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 72 BPM felt in 6/8, D major, a swaying waltz that lurches forward. Tender, then enormous.

VOICE: Male tenor with sand in it. Verses nearly spoken, close to the mic. Choruses pushed to the top of the chest voice with a crack on the highest note. No harmony until the final chorus, then one octave double.

INSTRUMENTS: Acoustic guitar in an open tuning where several strings ring the same note, giving a constant drone. Mandolin tremolo answering the vocal. A full string section that arrives late and takes over. Fretless-sounding melodic bass. Big, roomy rock drums with wide crash cymbals. Clean electric guitar doubling the drone.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, droning guitar and mandolin. 0:14 Verse 1, voice and guitar. 0:40 Pre-chorus, strings creep in. 0:53 Chorus 1, the band crashes in. 1:22 Verse 2, pulled back with mandolin answers. 1:48 Pre-chorus. 2:01 Chorus 2. 2:30 Instrumental, mandolin and strings trade the tune and the bar stumbles once, as if the song loses its footing. 2:52 Bridge, the hardest singing. 3:14 Breakdown, two lines with guitar only. 3:26 Final chorus at full size. 3:56 Outro, the band drops away and the mandolin fades by 4:10.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Late-90s radio rock: warm, wide and slightly compressed, strings mixed as loud as the guitars, vocal dry and forward.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The stumbling bar in the instrumental at about 2:40, followed by the whole orchestra lifting into the bridge.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The lyric moves the invisibility from a film angel to an ordinary room with a lit screen in it. A soft sub-bass sits under the choruses for modern speakers.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Longing, frustration, a plea, and at the end a quiet hand held out.

WHAT IT IS ABOUT

Someone has become invisible to the one person who matters, and is standing right there. All it would take is for that person to look up.

THE OTHER WAYS TO HEAR IT

Hear it as: a partner across the sofa from a phone; a parent of a teenager; a ghost or angel in the room; an older person the world has stopped noticing. Each fits every line.

ENGINEERED HOOKS AND THE DESIGNED MISHEARING

Borrowed mechanics: one plain sentence as the whole chorus, a narrator who cannot be seen, the lurching waltz and droning guitar, and a stumbling instrumental bar. Designed mishearing: 'If you looked up' is easily heard as 'If you looked, love', which turns a complaint into an endearment.
